knee_flex.source: e3rehab: "adjust the machine so your knees are bent as much as possible"; if the machine limits that to about 90 degrees, e3rehab says to use pads to bend further, so 90 degrees is the illustrative common-machine start; RitFit: "Terminal knee extension creates the highest patellofemoral contact pressure. Stopping a few degrees short of full extension is a practical modification" (illustrative 5-degree stop)

hip_flex.source: AmpAinSoc leg extension: "Hips stay seated — they do not lift during the rep" and "Glue the hips down throughout," a narrow band around the seated 90-degree hip angle

muscles.peakSource: RitFit leg extension guide: terminal knee extension creates the highest patellofemoral contact pressure, and quad effort is highest approaching that near-locked top, which is why the guide says to stop just short of it

mistake.name: Hips up, momentum up

tells.text: The hips lift off the seat as the weight gets heavy.
The leg bar is kicked up with a jerk and dropped back instead of a controlled extension.

mistake.source: AmpAinSoc leg extension: hips lifting off the seat is a "Sign of too much weight. Glue the hips down throughout"; Art of Manliness: "The big mistake people make with this exercise is bouncing/swinging the leg bar up, using momentum, and letting it drop back down"

sources: Contact fact (shin pad / ankle strap): the shin pad sits against the shins near the ankles on the machine's lever arm — a generic description of the part, not a numeric `machine.settings` value this research can cite
